findings.desc: missing-evidence-crash: analyze-batch.mjs main() computes generatedInputs via readFileBytes(paths.tamper) and readFileBytes(paths.resume) (plain readFileSync, no try/catch) at lines 176-177, which throws an uncaught ENOENT and exits nonzero with a raw stack trace (no report.json/report.md written, no FATAL input-integrity message) when tamper-verdicts.jsonl or resume-reconciliation.json is genuinely absent from the evidence directory. This directly contradicts the code's own documented contract one block above: the comment at lines 130-132 states tamper-verdicts.jsonl integrity is structural and 'a missing required field makes a hypothesis inconclusive, never a crash', and the comment at line 137 states 'resume-reconciliation.json: missing/empty => H3 inconclusive'. The adjudication logic (adjudicateH2/adjudicateH3) does correctly treat these files as missing via readTextOrNull => inconclusive, so the three-state adjudication itself never yields a false pass -- but the downstream report-generation step crashes before any report is emitted, an unhandled path inconsistent with the documented contract. selfcheck-m4.mjs sub-check G only exercises the present-but-EMPTY resume-reconciliation.json case (writes an empty string, not an absent file); there is no sub-check for a genuinely absent tamper-verdicts.jsonl or resume-reconciliation.json. Reproduced: copy only batch-ledger.jsonl+protocol.json(+.sha256)+lib/ into a fresh sandbox (omit tamper-verdicts.jsonl and resume-reconciliation.json) and run node analyze-batch.mjs -> throws Error: ENOENT at readFileBytes (analyze-batch.mjs:51) called from main (analyze-batch.mjs:176), exit code 1, no report.json produced.

H1 false-pass: adjudicateH1 (analyze-batch.mjs:221-258) treats a scale with >=2 proof records as checkable/pass-eligible purely by record COUNT, without checking that digests/goldMetrics are actually present. If every proof record at a scale has digests+goldMetrics stripped/undefined (malformed producer output that still carries verifyStatus), canonicalJson({digests:undefined,goldMetrics:undefined}) is identical across records, so pairwiseEqual is vacuously true and H1 verdict=pass even though NO real replay-determinism evidence was compared. This can flip overall to all-pass and assert the verbatim SS3 claim on zero real evidence. Reproduced: stripped digests+goldMetrics from all 3 full-scale ledger records (recordDigest re-signed so input-integrity still passes) -> H1 still reports pass, overall=all-pass. selfcheck-m4.mjs check C (lines 156-177) only tests digests VALUE MISMATCH between records, never digests/goldMetrics ABSENCE, so this vacuous-pass path is untested.
